title.narrative: Strengthening Early Childhood Development and Basic Education Systems to Support Human Capital Development in Eswatini Project

description.narrative: In order to improve human capital development outcomes, the proposed project aims to take a life-cycle approach using education as an entry point with a focus on two areas of intervention, namely, Early Childhood Care, Development and Education (ECCDE), and Basic Education. To this end, four components will be supported.The restructuring maintains the components as originally designed. omponent 1 aims to improve access to quality ECCDE services including by strengthening coordination and regulation of the sub-sector. The component will support interventions that aims to improve coherence in the management of ECCDE services by undertake mapping of ECCDE services providers as well as regular quality assurance assessment. In addition, the project will support the improvement of the quality of ECCDE services by developing a comprehensive package and rolling it out in selected ECCDE service providers. Component 2 focuses on improving quality and internal efficiency in Basic Education by supporting literacy and numeracy interventions in the early primary grades, integrating ICT in mathematics and science education in junior secondary grades and improving retention in secondary education, including by addressing demand-side and supply-side constraints. Component 3 will focus on strengthening key management capacities of the MOET, regional and local education offices as well as supporting the Project Support Unit (PSU) which will play a key role in the coordination and management of the project, including in key aspects of project operations (e.g., procurement, financial management, M&E, Environmental and Social safeguards). This component will add support to interventions that institutionalize the PSI/PMI Model of Science and Mathematics instruction in the Teacher Training Faculty of Eswatini University and the William Pitcher College of Education. Component 4 is a Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC), to enable timely response to crisis that may impact the education sector.
To strengthen education service delivery and management systems in the early years and junior secondary education
